quote.text: Keep the prospect of death, exile and all such apparent tragedies before you every day – especially death – and you will never have an abject thought, or desire anything to excess.
quote.author: Epictetus
quote.aiInsight:
• Parenthood:
    • By contemplating the finiteness of life, we as parents are reminded to treasure every moment with our children, fostering gratitude and intentional love even in ordinary days.
    • When we recognize that tragedies and losses are inevitable, we learn to model resilience and balanced desires, teaching our children the value of temperance and fortitude in facing life’s challenges.
  • Leadership:
    • The awareness of mortality and potential loss cultivates humility, encouraging leaders to make decisions that are mindful and just, without being swayed by ego or unchecked ambition.
    • Embracing the inevitability of hardship and loss can inspire leaders to foster resilience in their teams, guiding others with a calm spirit and an emphasis on sustainable, ethical progress.
  • Product Management:
    • Keeping the perspective of life's impermanence aids product managers in prioritizing what truly matters, ensuring that their innovations serve enduring purposes rather than fleeting desires.
    • This philosophy encourages a balanced approach to risk-taking, wherein managing potential losses and failures positions teams to build robust products that resonate deeply with users’ lasting needs.
